# `m.stocks.financials.cash_flow_statements`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Cash flow statements of US public companies, one row per filer and reporting period.

```python
m.stocks.financials.cash_flow_statements(symbols=None, *, timeframe=None, start=None, end=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Tickers whose filings to return; None, the default, for every filing. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and the rows of each one you delete leave the table. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |
| `timeframe` | `dm.Timeframe.ANNUAL`, `QUARTERLY`, or `TRAILING_TWELVE_MONTHS`; None, the default, for every timeframe. |  |
| `start` | The first period end date. | The first day or moment of the range. A date (text such as `"2025-06-02"`, a Python `date`, or a Deephaven `LocalDate`) means the day in the market's time zone: New York for stocks, options, and indices; UTC for forex and crypto; for futures, the trading session that ends that day. An instant is an exact time: a Python `datetime` with a time zone, a `pandas.Timestamp`, a `numpy.datetime64`, a Deephaven `Instant` or `ZonedDateTime`, or Deephaven time text such as `"2025-06-02T09:30 ET"`. Give `start` and `end` as two dates or two instants. A `datetime` without a time zone raises `ValueError`, and a calendar-date field, such as an ex-dividend date, takes dates only. |
| `end` | The last period end date. | The last day, or the moment the range stops, in the same form as `start`. A date includes its whole day, so `start="2025-06-02", end="2025-06-02"` reads all of June 2; an instant is excluded. Leave it out to read through now; a list dataset then sends Massive no end, so it also returns records still to come, such as dividends announced but not yet paid. |
| `sort` | The field to sort by, such as `"period_end"`. | The field to order the rows by, named as Massive names it, such as `"ex_dividend_date"`. Where the endpoint allows, name several, separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc`: `"ticker,ex_dividend_date.desc"`. This page lists the values the dataset takes. |
| `order` | The direction of `sort`. | The direction of `sort`: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. |
| `limit` | The most rows to return, in total. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |
| `filters` | Further endpoint parameters, such as `{"fiscal_year_gte": 2020}`. | Any other parameter Massive documents for this dataset, as a mapping from the parameter's name to its value, with each dot in the name written as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. This page lists the keys the dataset takes. A key it doesn't take, or one that has its own argument, such as `start`, raises `ValueError` naming the keys it does take. A date or time value takes ISO 8601 text, or any value `start` takes. |

## Plan access

Which of Massive's plans include this dataset, how recent its data is on each, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Cash Flow Statements (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Stocks Basic | Not included |
| Stocks Starter | Not included |
| Stocks Developer | Not included |
| Stocks Advanced | End-of-day, All history |
| Financials & Ratios Expansion | End-of-day, All history |
| Stocks Business | Not included |
| Financials & Ratios Expansion Business | End-of-day, All history |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The ticker the request named that the row lists in `Tickers`: a row that lists several of the named tickers appears once for each, so an article about AAPL and MSFT read for both is listed under each. A request that named one ticker gives it to every row. Null when the call named no ticker, and on a row that lists none of a request's named tickers. | REST |
| `CashFromOperatingActivitiesContinuingOperations` | double | Cash generated from continuing business operations before discontinued operations. | REST |
| `ChangeInCashAndEquivalents` | double | Net change in cash and cash equivalents during the period, representing the sum of operating, investing, and financing cash flows plus currency effects. | REST |
| `ChangeInOtherOperatingAssetsAndLiabilitiesNet` | double | Net change in working capital components including accounts receivable, inventory, accounts payable, and other operating items. | REST |
| `Cik` | String | The company's Central Index Key (CIK), a unique identifier assigned by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). You can look up a company’s CIK using the SEC CIK Lookup tool (https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/cik-lookup). | REST |
| `DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization` | double | Non-cash charges for the reduction in value of tangible and intangible assets over time. | REST |
| `Dividends` | double | Cash payments to shareholders in the form of dividends, typically reported as negative values. | REST |
| `EffectOfCurrencyExchangeRate` | double | Impact of foreign exchange rate changes on cash and cash equivalents denominated in foreign currencies. | REST |
| `FilingDate` | String | The date of the most recent SEC filing that included this period's data. This is not necessarily the date this period was originally filed. Because SEC filings restate comparative data for prior periods, multiple records can share the same filing_date. For example, an annual 10-K reports three years of results, and a 10-Q includes prior period comparatives. To find the original filing date for a specific 10-K or 10-Q, use the SEC EDGAR filings index endpoint (/stocks/filings/vX/index). | REST |
| `FiscalQuarter` | long | The fiscal quarter number (1, 2, 3, or 4) for the reporting period. | REST |
| `FiscalYear` | long | The fiscal year for the reporting period. | REST |
| `IncomeLossFromDiscontinuedOperations` | double | After-tax income or loss from business operations that have been discontinued. | REST |
| `LongTermDebtIssuancesRepayments` | double | Net cash flows from issuing or repaying long-term debt obligations. | REST |
| `NetCashFromFinancingActivities` | double | Total cash generated or used by financing activities, including debt issuance, debt repayment, dividends, and share transactions. | REST |
| `NetCashFromFinancingActivitiesContinuingOperations` | double | Cash flows from financing activities of continuing operations before discontinued operations. | REST |
| `NetCashFromFinancingActivitiesDiscontinuedOperations` | double | Cash flows from financing activities of discontinued business segments. | REST |
| `NetCashFromInvestingActivities` | double | Total cash generated or used by investing activities, including capital expenditures, acquisitions, and asset sales. | REST |
| `NetCashFromInvestingActivitiesContinuingOperations` | double | Cash flows from investing activities of continuing operations before discontinued operations. | REST |
| `NetCashFromInvestingActivitiesDiscontinuedOperations` | double | Cash flows from investing activities of discontinued business segments. | REST |
| `NetCashFromOperatingActivities` | double | Total cash generated or used by operating activities, representing cash flow from core business operations. | REST |
| `NetCashFromOperatingActivitiesDiscontinuedOperations` | double | Cash flows from operating activities of discontinued business segments. | REST |
| `NetIncome` | double | Net income used as the starting point for operating cash flow calculations. | REST |
| `NoncontrollingInterests` | double | Cash flows related to minority shareholders in consolidated subsidiaries. | REST |
| `OtherCashAdjustments` | double | Other miscellaneous adjustments to cash flows not classified elsewhere. | REST |
| `OtherFinancingActivities` | double | Cash flows from financing activities not classified elsewhere, including share repurchases and other equity transactions. | REST |
| `OtherInvestingActivities` | double | Cash flows from investing activities not classified elsewhere, including acquisitions, divestitures, and investments. | REST |
| `OtherOperatingActivities` | double | Other adjustments to reconcile net income to operating cash flow not classified elsewhere. | REST |
| `PeriodEnd` | String | The last date of the reporting period (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD). | REST |
| `PurchaseOfPropertyPlantAndEquipment` | double | Cash outflows for capital expenditures on fixed assets, typically reported as negative values. | REST |
| `SaleOfPropertyPlantAndEquipment` | double | Cash inflows from disposing of fixed assets, typically reported as positive values. | REST |
| `ShortTermDebtIssuancesRepayments` | double | Net cash flows from issuing or repaying short-term debt obligations. | REST |
| `Tickers` | String[] | A list of ticker symbols under which the company is listed. Multiple symbols may indicate different share classes for the same company. | REST |
| `Timeframe` | String | The reporting period type. Possible values include: quarterly, annual, trailing_twelve_months. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
